issues.reason: Both bounds sit on the same event symbol at full strength, so the KB entails (TimeAtMost sk_complete_1 (Month august)) — the deadline the sentence explicitly says was superseded — and an atom that is false at speech time is a defect however uncovered the construction is.

The proper-noun exclusion cited governs a multi-word NAME occupying the NP, not a capitalized noun used attributively inside the indefinite common-noun compound 'a Medicare drug package'; the parser exposed no modifier genus, so (Member sk_package_1 medicare_drug_package) and (Inheritance medicare_drug_package package) are both true and well-typed improvisation in gap territory, and the missing Name atom is the gap itself (no licensed encoding both fuses the modifier and keeps its symbol).

gaps_confirmed: a stated deadline revised inside the same sentence ('by August, then extended it to Oct. 17') — cessation covers only 'no longer / not anymore / used to' over eventualities, and nothing retracts or supersedes a time BOUND

an episodic, specific past bare-plural subject ('Republicans had pledged') — the determiner rule routes every bare plural to the generic Inheritance / distributing Implication, which cannot express a one-off past event

a proper-noun modifier inside a three-word common-noun compound ('Medicare drug package') — the modifier_noun rule is written for a two-word compound and is disapplied for proper nouns, leaving the modifier's Name with nowhere to go
new_gaps: the antecedent of 'extended it' is the deadline itself — a time bound is an atom, not a referable symbol, so pronominal reference to it has no target and must be re-aimed at the event

'pledged to complete X by August' puts a deadline on a control complement that the instruction set marks occurrence-neutral: TimeAtMost then asserts a bound on an event that may never occur, with no way to scope the bound to the pledge's content
repair_summary: Removed (: complete1_deadline_month (TimeAtMost sk_complete_1 (Month august)) (STV 1.0 0.99)) — the superseded bound, dropped rather than replaced since no licensed construct retracts a time bound; the Oct. 17 bound and every other line stand unchanged.
notes: The control-verb treatment of 'pledged to complete' (Theme link, subject control, no tense of its own), the past-perfect Before, and Patient on the extended occurrence all follow the instruction set. The original August deadline is content lost to the gap, not content refuted.
